correctness.rationale: The augmentation ideal J is preserved as the radical; its quadratic layer is generated by products of generators. A substitution is therefore specified by L and a quadratic shear, and is invertible iff L is. The shear group M=Hom(V,V⊗V) is additive, with action rho(L)C=(L⊗L)CL^{-1}. Squaring and conjugating in this semidirect product gives the kernel of I+rho(L) and its quotient by the image of I-rho(L), respectively. In odd characteristic the negative tensor signs give 2(n-v)^2v+(n-v)^2v+v^3 free coordinates; the choice of a v-subspace and a complementary subspace gives the multiplicity of L. The image is all the negative eigenspace because 2 is invertible. In characteristic two choose a basis on which L swaps r pairs and fixes s=n-2r vectors (replace a Jordan pair e,f with f,f+e when (L-I)f=e). On the tensor basis of V⊗V⊗V* it acts by a permutation with s^3 fixed basis tensors and (n^3-s^3)/2 transpositions. Each transposition contributes one kernel and one image coordinate for I+rho(L); a fixed tensor contributes one kernel coordinate and no image. Choosing im(L-I), a containing ker(L-I), and the induced quotient-to-image isomorphism gives the stated Gaussian-binomial multiplicity. This also checks r=0, s=0, the fixed-fiber qualification, and subtraction of the unique identity for exact order two. An independent direct linearization and finite-field elimination over all 3-by-3 square-one matrices gives totals 134561792 over F2 and 7626343628152 over F3, with 21 nonidentity rank-one linear parts of lift dimension 14 over F2, and 117 linear parts of each of lift dimensions 13 and 14 over F3.
residual_risks: Conjugacy here is only under the identity-linear kernel above a fixed linear part. No extension to higher truncation, semilinear automorphisms, or full automorphism-group conjugacy is inferred.
